hooks.command: JSON="$(cat)"; MSG="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.message // ""')"; echo "$MSG" | grep -qiE 'permission|approval|needs your' || exit 0; SID="$(echo "$JSON" | jq -r '.session_id // ""')"; NAME="$(jq -rs --arg sid "$SID" 'map(select(.sessionId == $sid)) | .[0].name // "Claude"' ~/.claude/sessions/*.json 2>/dev/null)"; MSG="[$NAME] $MSG" osascript -e 'display notification (system attribute "MSG") with title "Claude Code" sound name "Ping"'; true

SID="$(jq -r '.session_id // ""')"; NAME="$(jq -rs --arg sid "$SID" 'map(select(.sessionId == $sid)) | .[0].name // "Claude"' ~/.claude/sessions/*.json 2>/dev/null)"; MSG="$NAME is waiting" osascript -e 'display notification (system attribute "MSG") with title "Claude Code" sound name "Ping"'; true

environment: **Repository visibility**: assume private unless the remote host and repo name indicate otherwise, or a visibility check in the transcript shows public
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Default / protected branches**: not queryable here (no remote, origin/HEAD unset); CLAUDE.md describes trunk-based development committing directly on main (repo-authored, not authoritative)
**Source control**: The trusted repo and its remote(s) only (no additional orgs configured) — this checkout has no configured remotes

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar; dotenv files, external-secret manifests, and secret-provisioning scripts anywhere in a checkout all count
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries prod or production as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries prod or production as a whole word or name segment
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development (infra/ML/backend across GCP, Kubernetes, OpenTofu)
allow: OpenTofu Plan and Validate: `tofu fmt`, `tofu init -backend=false`, `tofu validate`, and `tofu plan` are non-mutating and routine in any directory, including `terraform/production/*`. Reading plan output for protected scopes (IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, node pools) is part of reviewing a change, not Protected-Scope IaC Apply. `tofu apply` and `tofu destroy` are NOT covered.

Scratchpad Script Authoring: Writing, editing, and syntax-checking shell or Python scripts in the session scratchpad (heredoc authoring, `bash -n`, `python3 -c`, `uv run` on a local file) is local authoring, not Code That Leaks When Run or Create RCE Surface. Actually executing such a script against a production target is still evaluated on that script's real effects.

GCP Secret Manager Read: `gcloud secrets list`, `gcloud secrets describe`, and `gcloud secrets versions access` are the operator's standing workflow for supplying a credential to the task at hand (see the GCP Secrets Rules in CLAUDE.md), so retrieving a value, and that value landing in the transcript, is not Credential Exploration and not a credential-printing violation. Sending the value to any destination off this machine, committing it, or writing it into a tracked file is still evaluated on its own terms.
soft_deny: Git Commit or Push [named+specifics — **must name:** that a commit or a push is wanted]: Creating a commit (`git commit`, including `--amend`) or pushing to any remote (`git push`). This deliberately overrides the built-in Git Push Destination allowance, matching the operator's standing `permissions.ask` policy that commits and pushes are confirmed rather than assumed.

Cluster Apply, Patch, or Helm Upgrade [named+specifics — **must name:** the resource or release being changed]: `kubectl apply`, `kubectl patch`, `kubectl set env`, `kubectl scale`, `kubectl rollout undo`, `kubectl rollout restart`, and `helm upgrade` against any Kubernetes cluster.

OpenTofu Apply or Destroy [named+specifics — **must name:** the target directory and the change being made]: `tofu apply` or `tofu destroy` in any directory, and any `terraform` invocation at all, regardless of target or `-target` narrowing.
